## Read in all CSV files - Initial

```{r}
files <- dir(path = "/Users/ellag/Desktop/PhD/academic_projects/3d_reconstruction/data/model_and_traj", pattern = "\\.csv", full.names = T)
out <- lapply(files, function(x) read.csv(x))
names(out) <- basename(files)

full <- lapply(out, function(x) bind_rows(x, .id = "column_label"))

full.df <- bind_rows(full, .id="column_label") %>%
  rename(Observation = column_label) %>%
  select(-c(R:B)) %>%
  separate(Observation, c("Observer", "ID", "time", "fps", "opt", "3d", "output", "csv"), sep = "_") %>%
  select(-c(time, time, opt:csv)) %>%
  unite("Subject", c(Observer, ID, fps), sep = "_") %>%
  rename(x = X,
         y = Y,
         z = Z) %>%
  mutate(Subject = as.factor(Subject),
         frame = as.numeric(frame),
         fps = ifelse(grepl("3fps", Subject), 3, 1),
         time_sec = (frame - 1)*(1/fps))
```



cleaning 3D tracks

# first load all raw data and compute speeds and turning angles to filter with, then plot raw data

```{r}
library(zoo)

df.traj <- full.df %>%
  # ensure time ordering
  arrange(Subject, frame) %>%
  group_by(Subject) %>%
  # compute 3D step vectors and step length
  mutate(dx = c(NA, diff(x)),
         dy = c(NA, diff(y)),
         dz = c(NA, diff(z)),
         dt = c(NA, diff(time_sec)),
         step_length = sqrt(dx^2 + dy^2 + dz^2),
         speed = step_length / dt) %>%
  mutate(speed_in  = speed,
         speed_out = lead(speed)) %>%
  mutate(# vectors defined
         vx1 = dx,
         vy1 = dy,
         vz1 = dz,
         
         vx2 = dplyr::lead(dx),
         vy2 = dplyr::lead(dy),
         vz2 = dplyr::lead(dz),
         # dot product
         dot = vx1 * vx2 + vy1 * vy2 + vz1 * vz2,
         # magnitudes
         mag1 = sqrt(vx1^2 + vy1^2 + vz1^2),
         mag2 = sqrt(vx2^2 + vy2^2 + vz2^2),
         # angle (radians)
         theta = acos(dot / (mag1 * mag2))) %>%
  ungroup()


# plot raw data using plotly

library(plotly)
conflicts_prefer(plotly::layout)

# first define ranges of x, y, and z for all trials to plot everything in same space.
xlim <- range(c(df.traj$x, df.traj$x), na.rm = TRUE)
ylim <- range(c(df.traj$y, df.traj$y), na.rm = TRUE)
zlim <- range(c(df.traj$z, df.traj$z), na.rm = TRUE)


# define a palette that works for all trials
library(wesanderson)
n <- length(unique(df.traj$Subject))
pal <- as.character(wes_palette("Zissou1", n = n, type = "continuous"))

fig <- plot_ly(data = df.traj, x = ~x, y = ~y, z = ~z, 
               type = 'scatter3d', mode = 'markers+lines', 
               color = ~Subject,
               colors = pal,
               marker = list(size = 2),
               line = list(width = 1)) %>%
  layout(scene = list(xaxis = list(range = xlim),
                      yaxis = list(range = ylim), 
                      zaxis = list(range = zlim)))
fig
```



# Now identify outliers (spikes) in the movement trajectory and plot them

```{r}
# library(caTools)
df.clean <- df.traj %>%
  arrange(Subject, frame) %>%
  group_by(Subject) %>%
  # first define the thresholds (s = speed, a = turning angle) for filtering outlier movement
  mutate(s = as.numeric(quantile(speed, 0.9, na.rm = TRUE)),
         a = as.numeric(quantile(theta, 0.9, na.rm = TRUE))) %>%
  mutate(spike_raw = if_else(is.na(speed_in) | is.na(speed_out) | is.na(theta), FALSE,
                             speed_in > s & speed_out > s & theta > a),
         high_speed = if_else(is.na(speed), FALSE, speed > s)) %>%
  mutate(run_id = cumsum(high_speed != lag(high_speed, default = FALSE))) %>%
  group_by(Subject, run_id) %>%
  mutate(spike_run = any(spike_raw) & high_speed | high_speed) %>%
  ungroup()


# plot the new trajectories with the outliers removed, but also show where those outliers were

fig.clean <- plot_ly()

subjects <- unique(df.clean$Subject)

for (s in subjects) {
  
  # Good
  fig.clean <- fig.clean %>%
    add_trace(
      data = df.clean[df.clean$Subject == s & df.clean$spike_run == FALSE, ],
      x = ~x, y = ~y, z = ~z,
      type = 'scatter3d',
      mode = 'markers+lines',
      marker = list(size = 2, symbol = 'circle'),
      line = list(width = 1),
      name = s,
      legendgroup = s,
      showlegend = TRUE
    )
  
  # Bad
  fig.clean <- fig.clean %>%
    add_trace(
      data = df.clean[df.clean$Subject == s & df.clean$spike_run == TRUE, ],
      x = ~x, y = ~y, z = ~z,
      type = 'scatter3d',
      mode = 'markers',
      marker = list(size = 2, symbol = 'x'),
      name = s,
      legendgroup = s,
      showlegend = TRUE
    )
}

fig.clean <- fig.clean %>%
  layout(scene = list(
    xaxis = list(range = xlim),
    yaxis = list(range = ylim),
    zaxis = list(range = zlim)
  ))

fig.clean
```


# now remove the outliers and interpolate over those locations instead

NOW I NEED TO REMOVE THE LAST POINT IF THEY ARE HIGH SPEED OR SPIKE RUNS BECAUSE THEY CAN'T BE INTERPOLATED

```{r}
df.interp <- df.clean %>% 
  mutate(spike_run = coalesce(spike_run, FALSE),
         across(c(x, y, z), ~ ifelse(spike_run, NA_real_, .))) %>%
  # remove old step_lengths and speeds and flag
  select(Subject:time_sec) %>%
  arrange(Subject, frame) %>%
  group_by(Subject) %>%
  # interpolate missing coordinates
  mutate(x = na.approx(x, na.rm = FALSE, rule = 1),
         y = na.approx(y, na.rm = FALSE, rule = 1),
         z = na.approx(z, na.rm = FALSE, rule = 1)) %>%
  # recalculate step_length and speed
  mutate(dx = c(NA, diff(x)),
         dy = c(NA, diff(y)),
         dz = c(NA, diff(z)),
         dt = c(NA, diff(time_sec)),
         step_length = sqrt(dx^2 + dy^2 + dz^2),
         speed = step_length / dt) %>%
  ungroup()



df.smooth <- df.interp %>%
  group_by(Subject) %>%
  arrange(time_sec) %>%
  mutate(x_med = rollmedian(x, k = 5, fill = NA, align = "center"),
         y_med = rollmedian(y, k = 5, fill = NA, align = "center"),
         z_med = rollmedian(z, k = 5, fill = NA, align = "center")) %>%
  ungroup()



fig.smooth <- plot_ly(data = df.smooth, x = ~x, y = ~y, z = ~z, 
               type = 'scatter3d', mode = 'markers+lines', 
               color = ~Subject,
               colors = pal,
               marker = list(size = 2),
               line = list(width = 1)) %>%
  layout(scene = list(xaxis = list(range = xlim),
                      yaxis = list(range = ylim), 
                      zaxis = list(range = zlim)))
fig.smooth
```
